component_findings.c_native: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-5--rust): Breadth and reliability of working, maintained external integrations: (1) official/major cloud-provider SDKs (AWS, Azure, GCP), (2) database drivers for major SQL/NoSQL systems, (3) messaging/streaming and RPC integrations (Kafka, AMQP, gRPC), (4) observability/tracing standard (OpenTelemetry) support, (5) CI/CD platform native support. Same dimensions and evidence approach (official SDK repos/docs, CNCF project pages, well-known crate ecosystem surveys) applied identically to all 10 languages; this shard scores only Rust.

component_findings.extension_embedding: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-5--rust): Rust's external integration coverage is strong and broad-based (official AWS SDK with full per-service coverage, official MongoDB driver, mature Redis/Postgres/MySQL crates, mature gRPC via tonic, and an official CNCF OpenTelemetry implementation) but is held back of a top score by the comparative immaturity of its Azure SDK (beta, narrow service list) and its fragmented/partly-unofficial GCP story, plus known gaps in individual drivers (e.g., historically missing GridFS support in the MongoDB driver, transactions initially unsupported).
component_findings.language_bindings: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-5--rust): Mature community-maintained drivers exist for the other major databases, e.g., redis-rs offering 'a full implementation of the Redis communication protocol' using tokio as the async runtime, alongside widely used Postgres/MySQL crates.

metric.implemented_platform_coverage.candidate_universe: web_search against official rustc book / Rust blog / historical internals RFC thread

component_findings.architectures: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-5--rust): Rust ships Tier-1 (fully guaranteed) support for Windows/macOS/Linux across the dominant architectures, Tier-2 support for iOS, Android, WASI (wasm32-wasip2) and dozens of ARM/embedded/server variants, and hundreds of Tier-3 targets spanning bare-metal microcontrollers, RTOSes, and exotic ISAs — one of the broadest implemented-platform footprints of any general-purpose language, trailing only C/C++ (via LLVM/GCC backends) in raw breadth, hence a high but not maximal score.
